accommodations.label: Specially designed adapted PE
accommodations.language: {child} will receive specially designed adaptive physical education 3x weekly for 30 minutes, delivered by a certified adapted PE teacher, with goals aligned to the general PE curriculum.
data_to_bring: Adapted PE or motor evaluation results
Notes or photos showing how {child} is currently included (or sidelined) in PE

accommodations.label: Modified equipment and rules in general PE
accommodations.language: {child} will participate in general physical education with modified equipment (e.g., lightweight or larger balls, lowered targets, ramps for bowling) and adapted rules so that {child} is an active participant, not a scorekeeper or observer.
data_to_bring: List of PE units for the semester
Suggestions from {child}'s PT or OT on safe equipment

accommodations.label: Adaptive sports and athletics access
accommodations.language: {child} will have an equal opportunity to participate in school athletics and intramurals, including information about adaptive and unified sports options, with reasonable modifications and accessible facilities for practices and events.
data_to_bring: Sports or clubs {child} is interested in
Any local adaptive sports program information

accommodations.label: Accessible field trip transportation
accommodations.language: For all field trips and off-campus activities, {child} will ride with classmates on a wheelchair-accessible, lift-equipped vehicle with four-point wheelchair securement and an occupant restraint; separate transportation will not be used unless the caregiver agrees.
data_to_bring: Past field trip notices and how {child} was transported
Wheelchair make and model for securement planning

accommodations.label: Advance accessibility check of destinations
accommodations.language: Staff will confirm accessibility of each field trip destination (entrances, restrooms, routes, and changing facilities) at least 10 school days in advance and share the access plan with {child}'s caregiver.
data_to_bring: A sample access checklist you would like staff to use

accommodations.label: Trained support staff on trips
accommodations.language: A trained adult familiar with {child}'s mobility, personal care, and health plan will accompany {child} on all field trips; caregivers will not be required to attend as a condition of {child}'s participation.
data_to_bring: Any emails asking you to chaperone so {child} could attend

accommodations.label: Individualized emergency evacuation plan
accommodations.language: {child} will have a written individualized emergency evacuation plan naming two trained staff members (primary and backup), the evacuation route, any evacuation equipment, and the designated area of rescue assistance; the plan will be reviewed with {child}'s caregiver at the start of each school year.
data_to_bring: Map of {child}'s classrooms and floors
Questions about elevator use during alarms

accommodations.label: Evacuation drills practiced with real equipment
accommodations.language: {child} will participate in every fire, lockdown, and shelter drill using the actual evacuation route and equipment in the plan, and staff will document each drill and any barriers found.
data_to_bring: Notes from past drills where {child} was left behind or excused

accommodations.label: Visual and tactile alerts
accommodations.language: {child} will receive emergency alerts in an accessible format (visual strobe alerts, a tactile or vibrating pager, or a designated staff buddy) so that {child} is notified of drills and emergencies at the same time as peers.
data_to_bring: Audiology or vision report
Description of how {child} currently learns about alarms

accommodations.label: Early release between classes
accommodations.language: {child} will be released 3 to 5 minutes early from each class to travel to the next location before hallways are crowded, with a peer or staff member of {child}'s choosing as needed.
data_to_bring: {child}'s class schedule with room locations
Timed notes of how long transitions currently take

accommodations.label: Elevator access and key
accommodations.language: {child} will have independent elevator access (key or card) and a backup plan if the elevator is out of service, including classroom relocation so that no instruction is missed.
data_to_bring: Dates the elevator was out of service and what happened

accommodations.label: No penalty for tardiness and a second set of books
accommodations.language: {child} will not be marked tardy or penalized for arrival times related to mobility, and will have a second set of textbooks at home to reduce weight carried between classes.
data_to_bring: Attendance or tardy records
Weight of {child}'s current backpack

accommodations.label: Assistive technology evaluation
accommodations.language: {child} will receive a comprehensive assistive technology evaluation by a qualified AT specialist, including trials of devices in real classroom settings, with results reviewed by the team within 30 days of completion.
data_to_bring: Work samples showing writing or access challenges
Apps or tools {child} already uses at home

accommodations.label: Device use at home and training
accommodations.language: {child}'s school-provided assistive technology device will go home daily for homework, and {child}, {child}'s caregivers, and classroom staff will receive training on its use, maintenance, and troubleshooting.
data_to_bring: List of homework tasks that require the device

accommodations.label: Alternative computer access
accommodations.language: {child} will have alternative computer access as needed (e.g., speech-to-text, word prediction, switch access, adapted keyboard or trackball) for all written work and assessments.
data_to_bring: OT report on fine motor skills
Examples of work that took far longer than peers

accommodations.label: Positioning equipment and schedule
accommodations.language: {child} will have access to appropriate positioning equipment (adapted chair, stander, or floor seating) and a position-change schedule developed with {child}'s physical therapist, with staff trained on safe transfers.
data_to_bring: PT recommendations on positioning
Photos of positioning that works at home

accommodations.label: Private, dignified personal care
accommodations.language: {child} will have access to an accessible, private restroom or changing area with appropriate equipment, and personal care will be provided by trained staff in a manner that protects {child}'s privacy and builds independence.
data_to_bring: {child}'s care routine and preferences
Doctor's orders for any health procedures

accommodations.label: Daily accessible transportation
accommodations.language: {child} will receive daily door-to-door transportation as a related service on a lift-equipped vehicle, with a ride time no longer than that of peers on comparable routes and a driver and aide trained in wheelchair securement.
data_to_bring: Current pickup and drop-off times
Wheelchair specs and any transit-tested seating information

accommodations.label: Inclusive recess
accommodations.language: {child} will have full recess time with peers on an accessible surface, with access to adapted play equipment and adult facilitation of inclusive games as needed; recess will not be withheld for therapy or to make up work.
data_to_bring: Photos of the playground surface and equipment
Notes on how often {child} misses recess

accommodations.label: Testing accommodations
accommodations.language: {child} will receive extended time (1.5x), breaks for repositioning, an accessible testing location, and use of the same assistive technology used during instruction for all classroom and standardized assessments, as permitted by testing rules.
data_to_bring: Recent test scores with notes on fatigue or time
Upcoming state or district test dates

accommodations.label: Orientation and mobility instruction
accommodations.language: {child} will receive orientation and mobility instruction from a certified O&M specialist 2x weekly for 45 minutes, including white cane skills, campus routes, and community travel.
data_to_bring: Functional vision assessment
O&M evaluation or a request for one

accommodations.label: Braille instruction and materials
accommodations.language: {child} will receive braille instruction from a teacher of students with visual impairments, and all classroom materials will be provided in braille at the same time peers receive print materials.
data_to_bring: Learning media assessment
Examples of materials that arrived late

accommodations.label: Large print and magnification
accommodations.language: {child} will receive materials in large print (minimum 18-point font or as recommended), access to digital magnification and screen-reading tools, and preferential seating with reduced glare.
data_to_bring: Eye report with recommended print size
Samples of materials {child} can and cannot read

accommodations.label: FM/DM remote microphone system
accommodations.language: {child} will use a remote microphone (FM/DM) system paired with {child}'s hearing aids in all instructional settings, including assemblies and PE, with daily equipment checks by trained staff.
data_to_bring: Audiologist recommendation
Hearing aid make and model

accommodations.label: Captioning for all media
accommodations.language: All videos, recorded lessons, and live virtual instruction used with {child} will include accurate captions, and transcripts will be provided when captioning is unavailable.
data_to_bring: Examples of uncaptioned media used in class

accommodations.label: Qualified interpreter
accommodations.language: {child} will have a qualified sign language interpreter for instruction, extracurricular activities, and school events, and caregivers who need interpreting will receive it for meetings and conferences.
data_to_bring: {child}'s preferred language and communication mode
Events where interpreting was not provided

accommodations.label: Travel training
accommodations.language: {child} will receive community-based travel training, including accessible public transit, paratransit applications, and route planning, with the goal of traveling independently to work or school destinations.
data_to_bring: Places {child} wants to get to on their own
Local transit and paratransit information

accommodations.label: Job sampling and work experience
accommodations.language: {child} will participate in at least three job sampling experiences per school year in fields aligned with {child}'s interests, with accessible worksites and any needed job accommodations.
data_to_bring: Interest inventory or career assessment
Hobbies and strengths {child} is proud of

accommodations.label: Self-advocacy and student-led IEP
accommodations.language: {child} will receive instruction in self-advocacy, including explaining {child}'s disability and accommodation needs, and will help lead part of each IEP or 504 meeting with support.
data_to_bring: A short statement or video from {child} about goals

accommodations.label: Age of majority and supported decision-making
accommodations.language: At least one year before the age of majority, {child} and {child}'s caregivers will be informed of the rights that transfer, and the team will provide information on decision-making options, including supported decision-making and less restrictive alternatives to guardianship.
data_to_bring: Your state's age of majority
Questions about decision-making supports

accommodations.label: Physical therapy in the home
accommodations.language: {child} will receive physical therapy in the family home and other natural environments 1x weekly for 60 minutes, embedded in daily routines such as play, bath time, and outings.
data_to_bring: A typical day's routine
Videos of {child} moving and playing at home

accommodations.label: Family coaching
accommodations.language: {child}'s caregivers, including grandparents or other relatives who provide daily care, will receive coaching from {child}'s therapists during each visit so strategies can be practiced throughout the week.
data_to_bring: Names of all regular caregivers who would benefit from coaching

ifsp: Write down your family's priorities and concerns in your own words before the meeting
List everyone who cares for your child day to day so they can be included in coaching
Describe your child's typical day so services can fit real routines
Request copies of all evaluation reports before the meeting
Ask where services will happen and request natural environments like your home or child care
Bring short videos of your child moving, playing, and communicating
Ask what equipment, such as seating or a stander, may be available
Ask about service coordination and who your service coordinator will be
Ask when transition planning for age 3 will begin
You may bring a support person, interpreter, or advocate
iep: Request a draft of the IEP and any new evaluation reports at least 2 days before the meeting
Bring a one-page 'All About Me' with a joyful photo of your child
Write your top three priorities for the year on one page
Review last year's goals and progress reports and note what worked
Bring outside reports from therapists, doctors, or audiologists
Ask whether assistive technology has been considered and write down the answer
Check that PE, recess, field trips, and transportation are addressed
Ask for an individualized emergency evacuation plan if your child needs one
Ask how progress will be measured and how often you will receive reports
You may bring a support person or advocate
Ask for prior written notice for any request that is refused
You do not have to sign at the meeting; you may take the IEP home to review
504: Write a short list of daily barriers your child faces at school
Bring medical or therapy documentation describing your child's needs
Request copies of any school evaluation before the meeting
Walk the campus route your child uses and note access problems
Ask about passing time, elevator access, and accessible seating
Ask how field trips, clubs, and athletics will be made accessible
Ask for a written emergency evacuation plan
Ask who will share the plan with every teacher, including substitutes
Ask when the plan will be reviewed and how to request changes
You may bring a support person or advocate
transition: Ask your young person what they dream about doing after high school
Request age-appropriate transition assessments in writing
Invite your young person to attend and lead part of the meeting
Ask which outside agencies, such as vocational rehabilitation, can be invited
Check that goals cover education or training, employment, and independent living
Ask about travel training and paratransit eligibility
Ask about job sampling and paid work experiences
Learn your state's age of majority and when rights transfer
Explore supported decision-making before considering guardianship
Ask about ABLE accounts and how earnings may affect benefits
